user_input:
Implement the user-confirmed full-site functionalization in the existing D:\stylemaria Spring Boot + static HTML/JS project. User confirmed scope: all existing customer and admin pages, with POS payments recorded manually (cash or GCash/Maya reference), no payment gateway. Preserve the existing MySQL database setup, current framework/UI patterns, and prior intentional behavior (customer custom order is a request for admin quote; admin publishes quote in-app, not email). No fabricated/demo rows. Existing custom-order submissions are now required to have USER session, attach requester_customer_id/name/email/phone/address, customer pages home/customize/see-all/track are role-protected, and order checkout ownership is checked; this work passed 39 Maven tests. Inspect and continue from that state; avoid reverting it.

Bounded objective: make all existing pages actually use persistent backend data rather than localStorage/static demo behavior, covering dashboard/custom request queue, customer account order ownership and quote/tracking, inventory stock/material actions, wastage logs, POS pending orders/manual payment records, reports/staff data, and Auto-BOM generation/quote persistence. Implement only behavior supportable by current UI; for any module whose business rules cannot safely be inferred, keep the UI explicit and avoid false success. Use MySQL schema/idempotent migrations and server-side authorization/validation; never trust browser-calculated amounts/ownership for persisted records. Update directly related docs and tests. Run focused tests then full .\mvnw.cmd test and report exact remaining gaps. Stop if a required business decision/credential is absent; report the specific blocker rather than fabricating behavior. Do not create or commit a git commit.
title: Full-site functionalization

assessment_snapshot.intro: The existing project is a single-module Spring Boot application with static HTML/JavaScript pages and an established MySQL setup:
bullets: The requested scope covers existing customer and administrator pages, including order quotes/tracking, inventory, wastage, POS manual payments, reports/staff, and Auto-BOM.
Preserve current framework and UI patterns, existing customer authentication/ownership checks, and custom-order in-app quote behavior.
No gateway, demo data, or git commit; existing 39 Maven tests must remain passing.

proposed_outcome: Make the existing customer/admin pages use validated, authorized persistent MySQL-backed data while preserving the current Spring Boot and static UI patterns. Keep unsupported business rules explicit instead of reporting false success, add idempotent schema changes and relevant tests/docs, and verify with focused and full Maven tests.
